To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the plate scanning information is much more informative than traditional link flow information, and that it can be used for the estimation of path flows and trip matrices, and for selecting the optimal subset of links to be observed.

the scanned link data is very informative for path and OD pair estimation, that the scanning should be done at the most critical links in the network, and that the scanning should cover a sufficiently large portion of the network.

the plate scanning information is much more informative for the estimation of path and OD-pairs than the traditional link counts and that the plate scanning can be used to estimate the path and OD-paires in the absence of the link counts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of reconstructing and estimating trip matrices and path flows, based on plate scanning observations and link flow information.
the following questions: (a) How can we reconstruct and estimate the path and trip matrix flows based on the information contained in the plate scanning data?
the development of a new method for reconstructing trip matrix and path flows from link flow observations and scanned data, based on a novel formulation of the path flow reconstruction problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methods proposed are very promising and should be applied to real data to assess the practical implications of their use.
the methods presented in this paper are very useful in the reconstruction of path flows and trip matrices.
the plate scanning data are much more informative than traditional link counts, and that the proposed methods are able to exploit this extra information in an efficient way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to reconstruct path flows, given link flow information, and how to estimate path flows and the trip matrix, given link flow and scanned information.
the proposed methods are able to provide a significant improvement in path flow and OD-pair flow estimation, compared with the traditional approaches, when one has access to the scanned data.
we have developed a new method for reconstructing trip matrices and path flows based on plate scanning, link flow observations and prior path flows.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, if the link counts are available and the plate scanning data are available, the latter can be used to reconstruct the path flow information.
, in the presence of scanned data, the link flow data can be considered as a noisy version of the scanned data.
scanning a subset of the links in the network is much more informative than scanning all the links in the entire network.
